hook.text: An algorithm predicts where crime will happen next. Police show up before any crime occurs.

buildup.text: Predictive policing uses historical crime data and AI to deploy officers to 'hot spots.'

discovery.text: Early pilots in Los Angeles showed reduced burglaries in targeted areas.

twist.text: The data reflects past policing bias. Over-policed neighborhoods get flagged again, creating a loop.

climax.text: Predictive policing doesn't predict crime. It predicts where police already look — and sends more.

punchline.text: Predict crime, or predict bias? The algorithm can't tell.

quiz.question: What is the main criticism of predictive policing algorithms?
options: They reinforce existing biases by using historically biased data
They are too expensive for most cities
They only work for minor crimes
